title: RAW-BER CONTRACT
status_reason: All 19 objections were accepted (0 refuted); none kills the relaxed-refresh core. The sense-amp flag leg is killed: a delayed strobe sees 50-150 ps skew against a 14-35 ps window, and even ideal flags net -2.2% to -0.2% of die. Keeping chipkill and moving to DDR5's real 32 ms window and post-on-die-SEC error structure cuts the commodity headline from 15x to ~9x at 85 C (6-20x; ~13x on retired DDR4; 2.9-4x in degraded mode). 64Gb refresh-busy recovery falls from ~38 to ~6-16 points, and the value is ~$3.9 per module over 5 yr. Provability falls from 'yes' to 'partly': raw 1b/1c maps need a vendor test mode, 2e-19 is bounded by census plus model, and the new-die sort flow stays on paper.

revised_verdicts.possible: Yes for relaxed refresh behind a side-band code: coding theory on measured retention tails, no new physics. No for the delayed-strobe sense-amp flag as specified (killed). Revival only with silicon flag-window sigma <=1.5 mV and a positive ledger.
revised_verdicts.profitable: Refresh energy and refresh-busy time, with chipkill kept: ~9x on DDR5 RDIMMs at 85 C (6.1x pessimistic, 20x optimistic, 17.8x without the DDR5 retention derate, ~35x at 65 C, 2.9x in degraded mode) and ~13x on retired DDR4 behind CXL (7.8x pessimistic, 4x degraded). Was 15x without chipkill. Module level: 0.98 -> 0.11 W per 64 GB, ~$3.9 per module over 5 yr. 64Gb refresh-busy 18% -> 2% (~6-16 points after same-bank refresh). Margin for new cells 1.88x (Cs 5.4 -> 2.7 fF), no flag bonus.
revised_verdicts.doable: Partly. Yes: DDR4 raw physics, DDR5 post-on-die-ECC statistics (JEDEC ECS counts + open Antmicro DDR5 RDIMM testers), VRT coincidence and dwell-time (RTN) spectrum, failure-mode census, 1 h-grade vs 1,000 h-hold servo test, and DDR5 + retired-DDR4 CXL soaks. Phase 1 decisive ~$124k at M6; $946k all-in over 24 months. No: raw ECC-off 1b/1c maps (vendor test mode), 2e-19 per read directly (census + coincidence model bound it), and the sort/repair flow for dies built to contract (paper study).

revised_experiment: Phase 1 (M0-6, ~$124k, decisive). (a) Retired-DDR4 raw physics on 4 DRAM Bender stations. 150 DDR4 modules are quick-screened across >=30 lots per vendor; 60 are deep-mapped across 1x-1a date codes for a node trend; 20 are rejects. Retention is mapped at 0.128-4 s x 45/65/85 C x 4 patterns, and the cluster spectrum is scored with RS-8 and BCH-12. (b) DDR5 leg: >=24 1a/1b RDIMMs on two open Antmicro DDR5 RDIMM testers. Per-die singleton counts come from JEDEC ECS codeword mode; post-SEC 2-3-bit event maps are added; BEER-style H-matrix recovery inverts them; and the RS-8-behind-SEC safe interval is computed. (c) VRT: per-codeword arrival counts per scrub period at 1 s/85 C over 1,000 h on 20 modules, plus a dwell-time (RTN) spectrum from row subsets re-mapped every 20 s-20 min. (d) Failure-mode census: every multi-bit event classified by chip/DQ/beat/row/column/MAT; event rates at 1 s vs 32/64 ms; first-read chip marking tested. (e) Servo/sort proxy: a 1 h grade per module must hold over 1,000 h. (f) Hammer at relaxed refresh with controller RFM. (g) Flag-proxy validation as revival data only. GO/NO-GO at M6. GO if the RS-8 (chipkill) safe interval including VRT is >=6x the part's JEDEC window at 85 C (DDR5 >=0.19 s, DDR4 >=0.38 s) and >=24x at 65 C; multi-chip events are <=10% with no new mechanism at >2x its 32/64 ms rate; and the 1 h grade holds for >=95% of modules. NO-GO if <4x the window at 65 C. Phases 2-3 (M4-18): Agilex CXL Type-3 controller on retired DDR4, plus controller RTL on the DDR5 tester. 1,000 h soaks at the servoed interval require 0 UE and corrected errors within 2x of model. Also measured: p50/p99 load-to-use at injected 1e-4, and self-refresh vs power-down + controller-REF power. One sky130 slot carries reset-on-REF counters and an amplitude-flag structure. Total $946k, 24 months.

responses.response: Valid. Reduced-tRCD failures track access-path timing: slow charge sharing, high access/contact resistance, subarray/column clustering (Solar-DRAM). The flag targets small |dV|, and these are different populations. The flag leg is now killed on circuit and bit-economics grounds: RT-CIRC-01, and RT-CIRC-02 (ideal flags net -2.2% to -0.2% of die; model 10.5). So GO-B is removed from the decisive gate and no decision rests on the proxy. As zero-hardware revival data, Phase 1 step 8 runs the critic's validation. Truncated-tRAS cells, whose |dV| is known by construction, are compared with reduced-tRCD flags: overlap, and column/subarray correlation of flags against random. An amplitude-domain proxy is added: two reads with opposite residual bitline offsets from a deliberately shortened tRP, whose disagreement set is |dV| < delta by construction [UNVERIFIED-PK method, FracDRAM/ComputeDRAM-style timing violation].
responses.action: GO-B (>=50% flaggable) deleted from the M6 gate. Proxy validation and a biased-precharge proxy kept in Phase 1 step 8 as revival data for the killed flag leg.

responses.response: Valid, and the model was worse than the critic said. DDR5's own JEDEC window is 32 ms (tREFI 3.9 us x 8192 REF), half of DDR4's 64 ms [REPORTED, resp log]. That is direct evidence the tail moved left. The original model also paired DDR5's tREFI with a 64 ms window. The model now applies ret_time_scale_ddr5 = 0.5 (1.0 as sensitivity) and places the controller code behind DDR5 on-die SEC. That hurts RS-8: doublets become 3-symbol events, so the internal limit falls from 5.4e-5 to 1.5e-5. DDR5 RDIMM with chipkill at 85 C: central 285 ms = 8.9x the 32 ms spec; pessimistic 194 ms = 6.1x; optimistic 643 ms; 569 ms without the derate; 1.14 s at 65 C. The DDR4 lognormal no longer sets the DDR5 interval. Phase 1 adds a DDR5 leg (+$28k): >=24 1a/1b DDR5 RDIMMs from 2-3 vendors on two open Antmicro DDR5 RDIMM testers (Artix US+; Google-funded; used for the Phoenix DDR5 study). It reads per-die singleton counts through JEDEC ECS codeword-count mode; the 256/Gb threshold masks only BER < ~2.4e-7 on a 16Gb die. It adds post-SEC 2-3-bit event maps and inverts them with BEER-style H-matrix recovery. The critic's raw ECC-off maps still need a vendor test mode.
responses.action: Commodity DDR5 headline cut from 15x (DDR4-derived, no chipkill) to ~9x central (6-20x) at 85 C. DDR5 leg on open testers added to Phase 1. New kill #9 on the DDR5 inference. Vendor NDA test mode pursued in parallel.

responses.response: Valid. The 1x/day VRT growth is an unsourced ESTIMATE (swept 0.1-100x/day), and the plan measured mean growth, not same-codeword coincidence. Model 10.7: if 10% of VRT error bits arrive as same-codeword pairs, the BCH-12 limit falls from 3.32e-4 to 1.02e-4, and to 4.6e-5 at 30%. RS-8 counts a pair as at most two symbols, so the chipkill path, now the headline, is insensitive. The kill #4 threshold is unchanged: ~700x/day still holds >=0.5 s with a 10-minute scrub on RS-8 (DDR4 basis). Phase 1 adds per-codeword VRT arrival counts per scrub period at 1 s/85 C over 1,000 h on 20 modules (overdispersion vs Poisson, folded into the 2e-19 calculation). It also adds a VRT dwell-time spectrum, the RTN-at-the-right-timescale measurement: row subsets re-mapped every 20 s-20 min at 85 C (<= 1/3 of the shortest dwell), plus hourly whole-module maps.
responses.action: Phase 1 step 4: VRT coincidence counts and a dwell-time (RTN) spectrum. The VRT pass line requires per-codeword pairs within 2x of Poisson.

responses.response: Valid: counting cannot reach 2e-19, and correlated mechanisms set the tail. First, RS-8 with chipkill is now the headline code. Any mechanism confined to one chip is corrected, such as a weak sub-wordline driver or a MAT-edge defect inside one die. The residual is coincidence: a chip-confined fault plus one random symbol error in another chip on the same read. Model 10.6 uses 30 FIT/die of multi-bit faults [UNVERIFIED-PK field studies], i.e. 0.0105 per module-year. UE = faults x reads-before-marking x q. q rises from 1e-6 at 64 ms to 1.0e-2 on raw DDR4 at a servoed 1.8e-5 BER. That gives 1.1e-4 UE/module-yr if the controller marks a chip on its first chip-confined correction, but 1.1e-3 (the whole budget) after 10 reads. Behind DDR5 on-die SEC, q = 1.7e-6, giving 1.8e-8. Second, the 'Poisson to 6 errors' check is replaced by a failure-mode census. Every multi-bit event is classified by chip, DQ, beat, row, column and MAT, and each mechanism's event rate is measured at 1 s vs 32/64 ms. 1.8e5 module-hours bound an unseen mechanism at <=0.15 per module-year, i.e. a UE share <=2.5e-7 on DDR5. On DDR4 that bound is 1.5e-3, so DDR4 needs a ~10x BER guard or more census. Multi-chip common-mode events (VPP droop, thermal slew faster than the scheduler) remain for fleet telemetry. The JEDEC grade is fixed only after >=1e15-codeword fleet data, at the raise stage.
responses.action: Failure-mode census replaces the overdispersion-to-6 pass line. First-read chip marking becomes a contract rule (new kill #10). Chip-fault coincidence term added to the model. Grade frozen only after fleet data.

responses.response: Valid. No published IGZO array retention CDF reaches 1e-6 at 85 C. rt-DEV and this response found only typical Ioff; Kioxia OCTRAM quotes <1 aA with no temperature or statistic. The '1e3-1e4x to the right' figure was a typical-Ioff ratio and is withdrawn as a tail claim. Oxide PBTI and hydrogen Vt drift (systematic, history-correlated) and RTN-like Ioff switching are additional error terms the grade must carry. The revival condition is restated as a measurement: an oxide or gain-cell array retention CDF to <=1e-6 at 85 C, >=10x right of Si at equal Cs, with drift and RTN terms characterised. Idea I-12627 adds a design lever: two series write devices square the tail only if defects are independent. Model 10.10, DDR4-anchor tail at the RS-8 limit: interval 0.84 s goes to 5.6 s at rho = 0, but only 1.8 s at rho = 0.1 and 1.3 s at rho = 0.3. The tail-correlation test is therefore the decisive measurement, and the lever does not apply to Si storage-node junction/GIDL leakage.
responses.action: Kill #1 revival rewritten as a measurable condition (CDF to 1e-6 at 85 C plus drift and RTN terms). I-12627 stacked-write route recorded, with its rho <= 0.1 requirement. The 1e3-1e4x claim is removed.

responses.response: Valid: same core as RT-DEV-02, from the process side. The DDR4 population is kept for raw spatial physics and adds a node-trend axis: 1x/1y/1z/1a date codes, fitted to extrapolate retention tail, cluster spectrum and VRT one generation. The new DDR5 leg measures the governed product on 1a/1b DDR5 RDIMMs. It reads per-die singleton counts from JEDEC ECS codeword mode and maps post-SEC 2-3-bit events. Their spatial geometry is visible because SEC events are chip-confined, and BEER/HARP-style H-matrix recovery inverts them to raw rates. The red-team model run shows the post-SEC structure is what matters for the commodity product: the controller never sees singletons, and RS-8 behind SEC tolerates 1.5e-5 internal BER vs 5.4e-5 on raw DDR4. So the DDR5 GO is computed on the post-SEC stream, which the leg measures directly. Raw 1b/1c singleton spatial maps, the critic's exact ask, need a vendor test mode under NDA. They matter mainly for the new-cell leg and are pursued as a business-development item.
responses.action: DDR5 leg (ECS + post-SEC maps + H-matrix inversion) and a DDR4 node-trend axis added. DDR5 gate set on post-SEC data (kill #9). Vendor test mode sought for raw maps.

responses.response: Valid for a fixed fleet interval, but the controller need not use one. It servos each rank's interval on its own corrected-error telemetry, keeping measured BER at 1/3 of the code limit. That is NAND-style adaptive trim, and it costs 0.73x in interval at the DDR5 tail slope (BER ~ t^3.4). Model 10.8 with lot retention scale lognormal: at sigma_ln 0.35, a fixed interval covering the 1-in-1000 lot is 97 ms (3.0x), while adaptive per-module gives a 6.1x fleet-mean cut. At sigma 0.7 it is 33 ms (1.0x) vs 5.1x. Proving a 1-in-100 worst lot directly needs ~298 lots, which $1M cannot sample. So the demo proves the servo instead: each module is graded from <=1 h of test, and the grade must hold over 1,000 h for >=95% of modules. The DDR4 quick screen is widened to 150 modules over >=30 lots per vendor (+$6k), to measure sigma_lot. 'Zero wafer starts' stays true. A vendor 1 s retention screen becomes an optional bin, not a requirement.
responses.action: Per-module servoed interval added to the controller; population widened to >=30 lots/vendor; servo pass line (1 h grade holds 1,000 h for >=95%) in the M6 gate. The fleet claim is restated as a distribution: ~6x fleet-mean vs 8.9x nominal.

responses.response: Valid: the new-die leg needs a sort/repair flow, and none was planned. Model 10.9 sketches one: pauses of 0.5/1/2 s x 4 patterns x 2 temperatures = 28 s, plus ~12 s of write/read passes. That is ~40 s per batch, ~0.08 s per die at 512 parallel sites [ESTIMATE]. The same maps give each die's cluster spectrum. 'Repair clusters, leave singletons' consumes fewer fuses than 'repair every fail'. VRT growth cannot be screened at sort; it becomes a lot statistic from sampled 24-48 h soaks. Per-die escapes are caught in the field by the controller's servo, first-read chip marking and PPR, as NAND controllers handle bad blocks. Per-die guarantees are therefore statistical plus field-adaptive, as in NAND. Validation within $1M follows the critic's criterion scaled to modules: grade from <=1 h of test, hold over the 1,000 h soak. Redundancy/fuse redesign and tester cost stay unquantified: a partner-stage task.
responses.action: Sort-flow test-time estimate added (model 10.9). 1 h-grade vs 1,000 h-hold test in Phase 1 step 6. Fuse/redundancy design deferred to the first DRAM partner and listed as unproven in the PROVABLE verdict.

responses.response: Valid. 64Gb tRFC input revised from 1600 to 700 ns central (600-800 range; 1600 kept as an upper sensitivity). This response's search did not confirm any 64Gb or even the 32Gb 410 ns value. Model 10.2: blocked time at 3.9 us tREFI is 15.4/17.9/20.5% at 600/700/800 ns, not 41%. At the revised DDR5 central interval (285 ms) it falls to 1.7-2.3%, so ~13-18 points are recovered on an all-bank basis, not ~38. The same fix to the refresh window also changes 16Gb at 1 s: 0.24% blocked, not 0.48% (model section 5).
responses.action: trfc_ns[64Gb] 1600 -> 700 ns in the RED-TEAM REVISIONS block. The 'defuses the 64Gb tRFC crisis' claim is restated as ~6-16 points of refresh-busy time recovered (after same-bank refresh).

responses.response: Valid, and fatal to the delayed-strobe flag as specified. Model 10.5(a): the 3.6 mV window equals tau*ln2 = 14-35 ps of resolution time. A strobe-timing error s shifts the effective threshold by exp(s/tau). 50 ps of skew is 6-40 mV of equivalent amplitude noise, and 150 ps is 68 mV to >1 V. Only a locally referenced strobe pair with <=15 ps skew and tau >= 50 ps reaches ~1.2 mV, inside the critic's 1.5 mV line. An amplitude-domain alternative (an offset-cancelled dual-reference comparator) at 1.5 mV noise still flags 82% of errors at 7.2 false flags per error. It saves only 10 of 90 check bits (Chase t=8 vs hard t=9), and RT-CIRC-02 shows even ideal flags are net negative. Phase 1's reduced-tRCD proxy cannot validate the circuit (RT-DEV-01).
responses.action: Kill the per-read SA flag leg (named leg: delayed-sample flag latch). Revival needs silicon with flag-window sigma <=1.5 mV across >=1k SAs at 85 C without trim, plus a positive ledger. One amplitude-flag test structure rides the single remaining sky130 slot as revival data. The controller keeps a generic erasure input (chip marks, XED-style hints) at no cost.

responses.response: Valid; the ledger kills the per-bit flag as a product feature. Model 10.5(c-e) at raw BER 1e-4 with ideal flags: 0.40 flags per 640-bit line. One position plus an overflow bit costs 11 bits and overflows on 6.3% of lines; two positions cost 22 bits. Flags save 20 of 90 check bits (3.9% of die bits). The cost is >=11 transport bits (2.1%), or one extra beat in 16 (6.25% bandwidth), plus a second SA latch (+2-4% die). Net -2.2% to -0.2% of die. Inside the fixed 128-bit RDIMM side band, BCH t=10 + 2 flag positions (122 bits) reaches 3.62e-4 vs 3.32e-4 for plain BCH-12. That is +9% at best with ideal, all-soft flags, and -7% with 1.5 mV comparator noise. Refresh-latched (confident) errors erase the rest. No protocol carries flags for free.
responses.action: Same leg as RT-CIRC-01: the flag interface is removed from the contract and the headline. Revival only if a measured new-cell ledger is positive (e.g. >=25% parity saving, per RT-IND-02).

responses.response: Valid: the 15x headline was the no-chipkill BCH-12 path. The headline now uses RS(80,64) byte symbols, which keep SDDC. Model 10.1: retired DDR4 at 85 C gives 837 ms = 13.1x central and 500 ms = 7.8x pessimistic. Degraded mode, with one chip marked dead (erasure decoding, limit 8.3e-7), gives 258 ms = 4.0x. DDR5 RDIMMs behind on-die SEC are worse, because SEC turns doublets into 3-symbol events (limit 1.5e-5). They give 285 ms = 8.9x central, 194 ms = 6.1x pessimistic, and 92 ms = 2.9x degraded (366 ms at 65 C). No code is known to us that gives BCH-12 random-bit capacity and SDDC within 128 bits. The Hamming bound does not forbid one (~2^83 random-12 patterns + ~2^67 chip patterns < 2^128 syndromes), so it is listed as an open coding question for the advisor. Degraded-mode rule: on chip marking, that rank drops to its degraded interval until service.
responses.action: Server headline restated as ~9x (DDR5) / ~13x (retired DDR4) at 85 C with chipkill, plus a degraded-mode fallback of 2.9-4x. BCH-12 kept only for non-chipkill tiers. Code question (SDDC + t~12 in 128 bits) assigned to the coding advisor.

responses.response: Valid for an always-on controller-REF policy. Model 10.3: the refresh saving while the controller issues REF is 0.865 W per 64 GB at the DDR5 central interval (32 ms baseline 0.98 W). With the critic's 0.3-1 W power-down background, always-on controller REF loses only if self-refresh residency exceeds ~87% at 1 W. That is a small loss, but a real one for deep-idle servers. The fix is a hybrid policy: idle ranks enter the die's own self-refresh (no saving, no loss), and the controller issues relaxed REF only in active/power-down states. Saving = 0.865 W x (1 - residency): 0.69 W and $3.94 per module over 5 yr at 20% residency; 0.43 W and $2.46 at 50%. A programmable self-refresh interval would recover the rest. LPDDR-style temperature-compensated self-refresh is a precedent [UNVERIFIED-PK]; that is a JEDEC ask. Phase 2 measures RDIMM + PHY power in self-refresh vs power-down with 1 s controller REF, as the critic asked.
responses.action: Hybrid self-refresh policy in the controller. Idle-saving claim restated to exclude self-refresh residency. Phase 2 power measurement added. Programmable self-refresh added to the JEDEC grade proposal.

responses.response: Partly valid. The 5.6-6.2% slow path is real for raw DDR4 at 1e-4, but nearly all of it is single-symbol errors that a syndrome lookup fixes in ~4 ns. Model 10.4: at 1e-4, 6.2% of lines hold an error but only 0.20% need Berlekamp-Massey. At the servoed RS-8 operating BER (1.8e-5), 1.2% hold an error and 0.007% need BM; the mean adder is 0.05 ns and p99 is on the 4 ns lookup. Behind DDR5's on-die SEC, ~0% of lines need any fix. So decoding does not push p95 onto a 15-30 ns path. The CXL hop itself (+70-150 ns) is real: the commodity product is a capacity tier, as section 1 already stated ('~100-200 ns'). DRAM-class latency for cells built to contract needs the decoder in the host memory controller, where chipkill decoders already sit, or on-die.
responses.action: Single-symbol fast path specified in the controller. Phase 2 measures p50/p99 load-to-use at injected 1e-4 plus an ASIC projection for a host-IMC decoder (pass line: p99 decode adder <=5 ns). Commodity product labelled a capacity tier; host-IMC integration named as the DRAM-class path.

responses.response: Valid on value. A model fix partly offsets it: DDR5's real 32 ms window doubles the refresh baseline to 0.98 W per 64 GB. The saving at the revised central interval is 0.87 W; with 20% self-refresh residency (hybrid) it is 0.69 W = $3.94 per module over 5 yr ($0.062/GB, ~4% of module cost), not $2.60. That is still a feature, and section 3 already concedes no piece is claimable alone. Under the founder frame, business size is not a kill. But the step-change claim is restated: the commodity leg is ~9x on refresh energy, ~23-29% of a 3 W idle module, worth ~4% of module cost. The larger values are conditional and partly outside the $1M proof: 64Gb refresh-busy ~6-16 points, and new cells at half Cs. Strategy: lead with the open grade, the measured error atlas and a servoed reference controller (contributed to OCP/JEDEC), license the firmware to CXL controller vendors and hyperscalers, and treat venture scale as contingent on a new-cell partner qualifying to the grade.
responses.action: Commodity value restated at ~$3.9 per module over 5 yr. The company thesis moves from 'controller royalty' to 'grade + atlas + reference controller, venture value via new-cell partners'. Licensee asks become raise-stage milestones.

responses.response: Valid. The flag leg is now killed (RT-CIRC-01, RT-CIRC-02): ideal flags net -2.2% to -0.2% of die, and a delayed-strobe flag sees skew, not signal. Leading the IP with it would put the strongest-looking claim on a negative-value feature that DRAM vendors control. The IP order changes. Provisional #1 covers the raw-BER grade and test method (BER + cluster spectrum + VRT growth + chip-fault coincidence, code chosen from the grade). Provisional #2 covers servoed latching-aware relaxed refresh with first-read chip marking and a degraded-mode interval. A flag filing is optional and defensive only. For new-cell margin, idea I-12302 (plate-strip sensing, ~135 mV vs ~14 mV) is a far bigger lever than flags. Model 10.10: Cs 0.30 fF for 50 mV and 0.15 fF at the contract's 26.6 mV, vs 5.42 to 2.68 fF on bitline sensing. But it has planar Micron prior art (US 5,991,216; US 8,009,460) and its own disturb questions. It is a portfolio margin route, not replacement IP for this dossier. Net: the IP is thinner and the defensibility claim drops.
responses.action: IP strategy reordered: grade/test method and servoed refresh first, flag filing optional and defensive. IP budget $45k -> $35k. I-12302 recorded as the new-cell margin route.

responses.response: Valid. With tRFC at 700 ns (RT-PROC-04), 64Gb refresh-busy time is 17.9% on an all-bank basis. Same-bank refresh and finer granularity hide an estimated 1/2-2/3 of it (5.9-9.0% equivalent) [ESTIMATE]. Relaxed refresh divides whatever remains by ~9x (DDR5 central), so ~6-16 points are recovered rather than ~38. The 64Gb crisis case shrinks to 'meaningful, not decisive'. Vendor reluctance to bless relaxed-retention bins is a business risk, not physics, and under the founder frame it is not a kill. The servoed controller (RT-PROC-02) works on standard parts without a vendor bin. It does run REF outside the JEDEC average-rate rule, so it is a hyperscaler-validated mode, like Meta's DDR4 reuse, until a grade exists. A vendor willing to sell a relaxed-retention grade is a raise-stage milestone.
responses.action: Strategic 64Gb claim restated as ~6-16 points recovered. Out-of-spec REF named as an adoption risk. Vendor relaxed-grade commitment moved to the raise milestones.

responses.response: Valid as an investor read of the original plan. First, the DDR5 leg measures the governed product's post-SEC error stream, which is what the controller decodes, on 1a/1b RDIMMs via ECS counts and open DDR5 testers. Raw ECC-off maps remain a vendor-NDA item. Second, the investor-grade deliverable becomes a running system, not an atlas. That means 1,000 h soaks at the servoed interval on DDR5 RDIMMs (controller RTL on the open tester) and on retired DDR4 behind the CXL FPGA, with 0 UE and corrected errors within 2x of model. Retired DDR4 behind CXL is the Meta/Marvell landing zone and gives 13x central with chipkill. Third, the delta versus SAFARI's decade of characterization is stated narrowly. It is a grade (BER + cluster spectrum + VRT growth + chip-fault coincidence) scored against side-band codes at 2e-19, plus a servo that holds the grade in-system. The oxide-coupon atlas is deferred to the AND-STACK/PIXEL-STACK partners.
responses.action: Demo redefined around DDR5 + retired-DDR4 system soaks. DDR5 leg added. Novelty claim narrowed to grade + servo. Vendor test mode and oxide coupons listed as raise-stage evidence.

responses.response: Valid in part. Retired DDR4 behind CXL is where the physics is best: no on-die SEC, and RS-8 with chipkill gives 837 ms = 13x central, 7.8x pessimistic and 4x degraded. But at server level the saving is ~0.45 W per 64 GB DDR4 module (64 ms basis), and the CXL hop adds 70-150 ns. It is a capacity tier, and the feature is firmware-sized. The plan no longer presents a $10-15M controller ASIC as the value path. The first commercial vehicle is licensing the servoed refresh + grade firmware into existing CXL controllers (Marvell, Microchip, Astera, Montage). An ASIC is built only if a new-cell partner needs one. Two design-in commitments cannot be bought with $1M; they are a raise-stage milestone that follows the soak.
responses.action: Section 7's '$10-15M ASIC' is demoted to contingent. Firmware licensing into incumbent CXL controllers is the first vehicle. Two design-in letters become a raise milestone.

corrections.by: study owner, after the red team
corrections.text: The retired-DDR4 figures in these responses (837 ms = 13.1x central, 7.8x pessimistic, 258 ms = 4.0x degraded; 5.4e-5 RS-8 limit; 1.1e-4 / 1.1e-3 chip-fault UE; 1.5e-3 census bound; ~700x/day VRT line for kill #4; 0.007% Berlekamp-Massey lines) gave DDR4 a 640-bit line with 128 check bits, the DDR5 RDIMM organisation. A DDR4 x4 ECC RDIMM carries 512 data + 64 check bits per 64 B line. Model section 10.11 now gives, chipkill kept, 85 C: two channels in lockstep (RS(144,128)) 698 ms = 10.9x central, 6.9x pessimistic, 7.0x with a chip dead, chip-fault UE ~1e-14; one channel (RS(72,64)) 258 ms = 4.0x, 3.4x pessimistic, no relaxation with a chip dead, chip-fault UE 1.6e-6 / 1.6e-5, and it cannot hold 0.5 s at 85 C at any VRT growth. Lockstep holds 0.5 s up to ~324x/day; Berlekamp-Massey stays at 0.007% of lines in lockstep and ~0% on one channel. Where a response compares DDR5 behind SEC (1.5e-5) with 'raw DDR4' (5.4e-5), read the 5.4e-5 as a raw 640-bit line. The 13.1x holds only if the controller spends 11.1% of DDR4 capacity on extra check bits. DDR5 figures are unchanged. See dossiers/raw-ber-contract.md section 12.1. The objections and responses are unchanged.
